Oakeshott is more sceptical about all political doctrine, including any doctrine of conservatism itself.
[2] Working definition: conservatism is the political doctrine that treats inherited institutions, practices and settled expectations
as a store of accumulated practical experience, and therefore places the burden of proof on those
proposing to redesign them — favouring gradual, corrective, reversible reform over comprehensive reconstruction from first principles.

groups.heading: IMPLICATION / VERDICT
